Act as the design sub-agent for this task.

Design a practical initial Bend 2 Vulkan wrapper like Rust ash in empty /home/aivv/Документы/projects/bend-vulkan. User requires Giulio2002/bend-collections src/math/u64.bend U64{lo:U32,hi:U32}. Installed Bend 2.0.37; run bend guide before Bend. Linux Vulkan headers and libvulkan, glslangValidator available. Bend effects: def Entry.load()->IO(Result<&1,&1,U32 & String,Entry>): import "./native.c"; import "./native.js". C spliced into compiled program, runtime io_node(e,CID(K),a,b), io_tup, io_done/io_fail, io_cstr and io_eff(CID(Entry.load),fn,0). FFI custom opaque handle types NOT supported (only Base File/Socket etc), so do not invent opaque foreign types. User-defined Type or Data constructor wrapping U64 can cross normal constructor ABI. Need ash Entry/Instance/Device dispatch, explicit Vulkan errors, structs/configs and true 64-bit sizes, real native integration (headless discovery/device/buffer memory roundtrip minimum); scalable generated binding path desirable, honest limited initial scope, avoid toy facade or entire renderer. JS may fail clearly native-only. Need laws in LAWS.bend and PROOF.bend. Native GPU Vulkan work sequential effects; parallelize independent pure work where useful. Read /home/aivv/.agents/skills/architect/references/runner-prompt.md and rationale-template.md; you are one of three already managed design runners, do NOT recurse into architect/arena or spawn agents. Artifact only design.md ~100 lines at /tmp/bend-vulkan-design/candidate-1/design.md. Usage first, type/signature sketch, module layout, explicit ownership/FFI handling (no unsafe pointer forging from constructors), error cleanup and design alternatives. No repo edits.
I’ll read the Bend guide and the design-runner instructions, then write the design artifact with API sketches, native handle ownership, and a runnable initial scope.

The required U64 type is available locally, and the Linux headers include the needed discovery and memory APIs. I’m using the architect runner guidance to shape the API around affine dispatch contexts and checked native handle IDs; Bend constructors will never contain Vulkan pointers.

The design now keeps buffer creation, memory allocation, binding, and mapped I/O separate. Operations return the dispatch context even on failure so callers can clean up. The first integration test will cover real Vulkan allocation and byte readback; GPU command submission will be a later step.

*** Add File: /tmp/bend-vulkan-design/candidate-1/design.md
+# Bend Vulkan: checked native handles, explicit dispatch and allocation
+
+## Usage (caller's view)
+
+Import `src/vulkan.bend as Vk`; import the pinned `Giulio2002/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend as W` for every Vulkan size and offset. These are signature-oriented IO fragments, not a claim that tuple binding below is compilable Bend. `R<A>` means `Result<&1, &1, Error, A>`; every result is explicitly matched before continuing.
+
+```text
+# Discovery: retain each returned owner even when the result is Fail.
+e <- IO.try(Entry, Entry.load())
+(e, instance_result) <- Entry.create_instance(e, InstanceCreateInfo.default("headless"))
+(i, devices_result) <- Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(i)
+(i, properties_result) <- Instance.physical_device_properties(i, physical)
+(i, families_result) <- Instance.queue_family_properties(i, physical)
+(i, memory_result) <- Instance.memory_properties(i, physical)
+
+# Explicit device/configuration; physical comes from discovery, family from its snapshot.
+(i, device_result) <- Instance.create_device(i, physical, DeviceCreateInfo.single_queue(family))
+(d, buffer_result) <- Device.create_buffer(d, BufferCreateInfo.transfer(U64{4096, 0}))
+(d, requirements_result) <- Device.buffer_memory_requirements(d, buffer)
+memory_type = MemoryProperties.find_type(properties, requirements.memory_type_bits, HOST_VISIBLE | HOST_COHERENT)
+(d, memory_result) <- Device.allocate_memory(d, MemoryAllocateInfo{requirements.size, memory_type})
+(d, bound_result) <- Device.bind_buffer_memory(d, buffer, memory, U64{0, 0})
+
+# Actual Vulkan memory; each successful result supplies the next named value.
+(d, mapping_result) <- Device.map_memory(d, memory)
+(d, write_result) <- Device.write_mapped(d, mapping, U64{0, 0}, [0, 255, 17, 42])
+(d, read_result) <- Device.read_mapped(d, mapping, U64{0, 0}, 4)
+(d, unmap_result) <- Device.unmap_memory(d, mapping)
+(d, destroyed_result) <- Device.destroy_buffer(d, buffer)
+(d, freed_result) <- Device.free_memory(d, memory)
+cleanup_result <- Entry.close_tree(e)  # Also called after any intermediate failure.
+```
+
+Executable examples expand the matches into small continuation functions, as Bend requires matching computed results through parameters. Keep the first application error while separately reporting cleanup failures. Do not use `IO.try` after acquiring resources: it exits before cleanup. A successful `close_tree` invalidates descendant tokens; drop their Bend values.
+
+## Problem
+
+Build an ash-shaped Linux native Vulkan 1.0 subset on Bend 2.0.37: distinct Entry/Instance/Device dispatch, ordinary configuration records, exact result codes, discovery and explicit buffer/memory operations. Bend has no extensible opaque foreign-handle ABI, and affine constructors can still be forged or dropped. Native lifetime and pointer validity therefore require checked registry records, rather than a fictitious foreign type or integer-to-pointer conversion.
+
+## Shape
+
+```text
+import ../deps/bend-collections/src/math/u64.bend as W
+type Entry is Type:          Entry{id: W.U64}
+type Instance is Type:       Instance{id: W.U64}
+type Device is Type:         Device{id: W.U64}
+# Each following type is Data with one id:W.U64 field and its own constructor:
+PhysicalDevice; Buffer; DeviceMemory; Mapping
+type Error is Data:
+  Vulkan{command: String, code_bits: U32}  # Exact int32_t VkResult bit pattern, including unknown codes.
+  Host{operation: String, code: U32, message: String}
+  InvalidHandle{kind: String}; InvalidArgument{field: String}; Unsupported{feature: String}
+  ChildrenLive{kind: String}; EnumerationUnstable{command: String}
+# Configuration/query records are Data; no C pointers or sType/pNext fields escape.
+ApplicationInfo{application_name:String, application_version:U32, engine_name:String, engine_version:U32, api_version:U32}
+InstanceCreateInfo{application:ApplicationInfo, layers:List<String>, extensions:List<String>}
+QueueCreateInfo{family:U32, priorities:List<F32>}
+DeviceCreateInfo{queues:List<QueueCreateInfo>, extensions:List<String>}
+BufferCreateInfo{size:W.U64, usage:U32}  # Initially exclusive sharing, flags=0.
+MemoryRequirements{size:W.U64, alignment:W.U64, memory_type_bits:U32}
+MemoryAllocateInfo{allocation_size:W.U64, memory_type_index:U32}
+PhysicalDeviceProperties; QueueFamilyProperties; MemoryProperties; MemoryType; MemoryHeap
+def Entry.load() -> IO(Result<&1, &1, U32 & String, Entry>):
+  import "./native.c"
+  import "./native.js"
+Entry.create_instance(e:Entry, cfg:InstanceCreateInfo) -> IO(Entry & R<Instance>)
+Entry.instance_layers/instance_extensions(e:Entry) -> IO(Entry & R<List<respective properties>>)
+Instance.enumerate_physical_devices(i:Instance) -> IO(Instance & R<List<PhysicalDevice>>)
+Instance.physical_device_properties/queue_family_properties/memory_properties(i:Instance, p:PhysicalDevice) -> IO(Instance & R<respective snapshot>)
+Instance.create_device(i:Instance, p:PhysicalDevice, cfg:DeviceCreateInfo) -> IO(Instance & R<Device>)
+Device.create_buffer/allocate_memory(d:Device, cfg:respective config) -> IO(Device & R<respective handle>)
+Device.buffer_memory_requirements(d:Device, b:Buffer) -> IO(Device & R<MemoryRequirements>)
+Device.bind_buffer_memory(d:Device, b:Buffer, m:DeviceMemory, offset:W.U64) -> IO(Device & R<Unit>)
+Device.map_memory(d:Device, m:DeviceMemory) -> IO(Device & R<Mapping>)  # Whole allocation initially.
+Device.write_mapped(d:Device, view:Mapping, offset:W.U64, bytes:List<U32>) -> IO(Device & R<Unit>)
+Device.read_mapped(d:Device, view:Mapping, offset:W.U64, count:U32) -> IO(Device & R<List<U32>>)
+Device.flush_mapped/invalidate_mapped/unmap_memory(d:Device, view:Mapping) -> IO(Device & R<Unit>)
+Device.destroy_buffer/free_memory(d:Device, handle:respective handle) -> IO(Device & R<Unit>)
+Device.wait_idle(d:Device) -> IO(Device & R<Unit>)
+Device.destroy(d:Device) -> IO(Result<&1, &1, Error & Device, Unit>)
+Instance.destroy/Entry.unload/Entry.close_tree(owner) -> IO(Result<&1, &1, Error & owner_type, Unit>)
+```
+
+The type block abbreviates separate declarations/signatures; it introduces no new Bend syntax. Device creation enables no optional feature bits initially. Query snapshots expose names, IDs, API version, queue flags/counts, memory flags/types/heaps and relevant limits with their correct widths. Caller code chooses devices, queue families and memory types; the wrapper hides loader dispatch, ABI layout and temporary storage. This is a small, deep interface per boundary-discipline, with explicit Vulkan allocation policy rather than a renderer framework.
+
+Native records contain the real `Vk*` values and `PFN_vk*` tables. Entry loads `libvulkan.so.1` with `dlopen`, obtains `vkGetInstanceProcAddr`, then global commands; Instance loads its commands through that function; Device loads its commands through `vkGetDeviceProcAddr`. Required missing symbols produce errors before publishing an owner. Native parent links keep the loader alive; ordinary parent destruction refuses live owned children. Physical-device records are borrowed and invalidated with their instance. [Dispatch reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetInstanceProcAddr.html).
+
+Each constructor contains a registry ID `U64{slot,generation}`, never a pointer or raw Vulkan handle. Resolve slot bounds, generation, object kind, liveness and parent ownership before every native call; retire slots when generation would wrap. Registry records track buffer bindings and mappings, so wrong-device use, stale copies, freeing bound/mapped memory and double destruction return errors without reaching Vulkan. Affine dispatch owners reduce accidental misuse; they are not a security boundary or a destructor guarantee. This puts the invariant in one boundary, per encode-lessons-in-structure.
+
+Marshal constructors using the runtime constructor ABI (`io_node(e,CID(K),a,b)`, `io_tup`, `io_done/io_fail`, `io_cstr`); register effects using the supplied `io_eff(CID(Entry.load),fn,0)` ABI, verified against emitted C. C imports are spliced into the program, so shared native code is included once and registrations are emitted only for reachable effects. Build typed C structs against `<vulkan/vulkan.h>`; initialize `sType`, `pNext=NULL`, counts and pointers there. Validate embedded NULs, queue bounds/priorities, list lengths and allocation failures; free all temporary strings/arrays on every branch. JS effects return a clear native-only error with the same result/state shape.
+
+Use precisely upstream `W.U64{lo:U32,hi:U32}` for sizes, offsets, alignments and heap sizes. Reconstruct C values with `((uint64_t)hi << 32) | lo`; split both limbs on return. Implement unsigned lexicographic comparison where needed; upstream `le_signed` is unsuitable. Check ranges with subtraction after validating the start, and check `SIZE_MAX` before pointer arithmetic. Byte values must be 0..255. `count:U32` limits each copied chunk, not allocations or offsets; there is no fake 32-bit `VkDeviceSize`.
+
+Mapping stores the returned pointer in its native registry record and exposes only checked byte copies relative to the mapping. Initially map the complete allocation; flush/invalidate the complete mapping with offset zero and `VK_WHOLE_SIZE`, avoiding partial noncoherent atom alignment policy. Copies are bounds checked and serialized; map/unmap state and HOST_VISIBLE are validated. The example selects coherent memory; noncoherent callers explicitly flush after host writes and invalidate only after the necessary synchronization. [Mapping reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkMapMemory.html), [invalidation reference](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges.html).
+
+Enumerations use count/query/retry on `VK_INCOMPLETE`, accepting only a complete snapshot, with bounded retries and overflow-checked native allocation. Failed creates roll back unpublished Vulkan objects and registry reservations. Explicit destroy checks dependencies; `close_tree` walks live records in dependency order: establish device idle, unmap, destroy buffers, free memory, destroy devices/instances, unload. If idle cannot be established and the error does not permit teardown, return the surviving Entry for retry. Partial cleanup updates records immediately, making retries safe; preserve the original operation error separately. Dropping a Bend value alone releases no native object.
+
+Only the IO event loop mutates native records; no Vulkan calls enter Bend parallel evaluation or GPU `!` calls. Distinct Entry trees have separate owned state behind a small ID router. Collect discovery snapshots sequentially, then use balanced parallel calls for independent pure device scoring and payload generation. This satisfies parallelism without racing dispatch, mappings or cleanup.
+
+## Modules and generated path
+
+`src/vulkan.bend` exports the public surface; `src/vk/types.bend` holds records/errors/handle constructors; `src/vk/memory.bend` holds pure selection and checked-size helpers; `src/vk/native.c` owns loader, registry, marshalling and effects; `src/vk/native.js` implements explicit unsupported results. Calls cross at most public API → native bridge → Vulkan. Keep generated declarations in `src/vk/generated.bend` and dispatch metadata in `src/vk/generated.h`.
+
+`tools/generate.py` reads pinned Khronos `vk.xml` plus `bindings.json` listing supported commands and ownership/marshalling annotations. Generate constants/result names, typed dispatch tables and Bend effect declarations; handwrite registry and supported struct marshalling. Reject an allowlisted command with an unsupported field shape rather than emitting placeholder wrappers. Check in generated output with registry revision/hash; `--check` detects drift. Header layouts remain C's responsibility. Add commands in verified vertical slices; this scales beyond a manually maintained command list without promising all Vulkan.
+
+## Proofs and practical acceptance
+
+`LAWS.bend` records pure invariants: both U64 limbs survive size conversions; unsigned ordering honors the high limb; selected memory types satisfy the bitmask/required-flags predicate; checked ranges reject overflow. `PROOF.bend` imports LAWS and supplies actual proofs. Keep this import graph free of native effects; state explicitly that proofs do not verify drivers, C marshalling or cleanup. Run `bend PROOF.bend` before committing, and never silence a failed law with `@unsafe`.
+
+Native integration builds and runs a Bend executable that enumerates devices/families/memory, creates a logical device, creates and binds a buffer, writes/reads exact bytes, and explicitly cleans up. This proves real Vulkan host-memory integration, not GPU command execution. Use an available hardware ICD or Lavapipe; no loader/device is a clearly reported unavailable test, never a pass. Exercise unknown/stale/wrong-parent IDs, failed-create rollback, live-child refusal, bound/mapped free refusal, and callback U64 roundtrips above 2^32 without huge allocations. Run with validation layers when present and compare registry live counts before/after both successful and induced-failure paths.
+
+## Tradeoffs accepted and alternatives considered
+
+We accept checked Data resource IDs and copy-based mapped IO for a supported Bend ABI and controlled pointer lifetimes. We accept explicit destruction and native dependency checks because Bend affine values may be dropped. We accept a Vulkan 1.0 headless subset, whole-allocation maps and disabled optional features before adding shaders, command submission, synchronization, WSI, extension pNext chains or callbacks. glslangValidator becomes useful in a subsequent independently verified compute-submission slice.
+
+Rejected: raw U64 Vulkan handles cast back to pointers exposes lifetime/forgery hazards and platform handle representation. Rejected: one `run_compute` facade hides so much configuration that it cannot support independent resource management or later ash-like growth. Rejected: fully linear parent/child typestate trees make every query and failed allocation rebuild an expanding ownership tuple; checked native relationships provide better interface depth within Bend's actual ABI. Ash's explicit dispatch and destruction remain the inspiration, not its Rust borrowing machinery. [Ash Entry reference](https://docs.rs/ash/latest/ash/struct.Entry.html).
+
+## Open questions and next implementation step
+
+Which optional core features and submission commands should the next vertical slice expose? Can installed runtime helper sources differ from the ABI emitted by Bend 2.0.37? Resolve the latter first with a tiny compiled constructor-return probe carrying a nonzero U64 high limb and the actual IO callback registration; inspect emitted C, then implement the registry-backed Entry/Instance discovery slice. Synthesis is reserved for the managing orchestrator; this candidate makes no repository edits.
*** End Patch"));
